name: LTV to CAC Ratio
description: Determine whether the lifetime value of a customer justifies what it costs to acquire them.
formula: LTV = (ARPU x Gross Margin) / Monthly Churn Rate; LTV:CAC = LTV / CAC
business_contexts: a subscription software business reviewing its growth spend
a meal-kit company evaluating whether to keep scaling paid acquisition
a mobile fitness app assessing the return on its marketing budget
a telecom operator reviewing prepaid subscriber economics
an online education platform questioning its cost per enrolment
question_patterns: What is the ratio of customer lifetime value to acquisition cost?
For every dollar spent acquiring a customer, how much lifetime value comes back?
Does the lifetime value of a customer justify the current acquisition cost?
What is the LTV to CAC ratio at current churn and margin?
solution_logic: Step 1: Monthly gross profit per customer = arpu_monthly x gross_margin_pct
Step 2: Average customer lifetime in months = 1 / monthly_churn_rate
Step 3: Customer LTV = monthly gross profit x average lifetime
Step 4: LTV to CAC ratio = LTV / cac
key_insight: Lifetime value must be measured on gross profit, not revenue. Acquiring customers profitably depends on margin and retention, not top-line price.
common_mistakes: Using revenue instead of gross profit, which overstates LTV substantially
Forgetting that average lifetime is the inverse of churn, not a given number of months
Judging acquisition spend on CAC alone without comparing it to LTV
framework_soundbite: Lifetime value is monthly gross profit divided by churn. Compare it to acquisition cost before scaling spend.
